exposure: First trimester maternal BMI (underweight, normal, overweight, obese)
outcome: Maternal complications (pregnancy-related hypertension, gestational diabetes, severe anemia, postpartum hemorrhage, wound sepsis)
Neonatal outcomes (intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR), small for gestational age (SGA), macrosomia)
cohort: The study recruited 180 women with singleton pregnancies who were attending Nalanda Medical College & Hospital, Patna, Bihar, India.
finding: Both low and high maternal BMI in the first trimester are associated with negative pregnancy outcomes, including various maternal complications and adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Rates of Cesarean delivery increased with higher maternal BMI.
birth_weight: Neonates of underweight mothers tended to be SGA (small for gestational age) and neonates of obese mothers had an increased incidence of macrosomia.
